replies.reply:
OPTIONS:
- Fetch a poker from a hearth in town and jam the Great Gear anyway (for: making sure the clock can't strike thirteen, and paying Ambrose back with work)
- Go down to the square and find Pip and Hester, to see the shadows are truly back (for: knowing the children are well)
* Put the whistle back in Ambrose's hand, since the shadows are free and it was never spent (for: owing him nothing for something I didn't use)
DO: I hold the whistle out to Ambrose, slow. "Shadows are loose without it. Hester pulled the cork. It's Maudie's, and it wasn't spent. Fair's fair, it goes back to you." I wait with my hand open till he takes it.
JOURNAL: He gave it free and told me not to bring it back, and that sat on me like a debt. The whistle bought nothing, so giving it back is the only fair way to keep from owing him. Next I'll see about the clock, since it still runs fast.
NO LONGER: I still need to fetch a poker and get the whistle before midnight.
NO LONGER: Tibbersnatch carries the jar with him and leaves at midnight.
NO LONGER: He will hand over the jar for an old tin whistle, loved fifty years, its tune worn soft.

OPTIONS:
- Go south to the Lopsided Square, get the whistle to the peddler and the jar back (for: freeing the children's shadows)
- Climb up to the Gearloft and look at the Great Gear (for: knowing exactly where the iron has to go)
* Go south to the square, knock at a house, and buy a hearth poker for my buttons (for: iron to jam the Great Gear, so the clock can't strike thirteen)
- Stay and ask Ambrose how long is left (for: knowing how much time I have)
DO: I close my hand on the whistle and put it in my coat. "Ambrose. You gave it free, and that sits heavy on me, but I'll carry it right. Now I fetch iron." I go out the south door into the square to find a house with a poker, and I'll count out buttons for it.
JOURNAL: The whistle is in my hand, so the poker is the next job. A house will have one to spare for my buttons, and I'll pay fair so I owe no one. Iron in the gear keeps the clock honest whatever the peddler does, and the children stay safe.
NO LONGER: I still need to fetch a poker and get the whistle before midnight.

OPTIONS:
- Give the whistle back to Ambrose, since the shadows are free and the peddler never needed it (for: setting right what I took, so I owe him nothing and he keeps Maudie's whistle)
- Climb to the gearloft and wedge a poker in the Great Gear anyway (for: making certain the clock can't strike thirteen)
- Go down to the Lopsided Square to see the children and Pip with my own eyes (for: knowing the shadows really are home)
- Go back to the coal yard and count my sock (for: rest, and getting on with saving for a door that locks)
* Give the whistle back to Ambrose and tell him plain what has happened (for: settling the debt and returning what was dear to him)
DO: I hold out the whistle to Ambrose, slow. "The shadows are home, Ambrose, the jar's open and the peddler's gone. He never needed this. Fair's fair, it's yours. You said don't bring it back, but I'll not keep what I never spent." I put it in his oily hand and wait.
JOURNAL: The whistle cost Ambrose more than any button, and I won't carry it when the trade didn't happen. Giving it back is the nearest I can get to even with him. After that I'll go back to the coal and the sock and the four walls I'm saving for.
NO LONGER: I still need to fetch a poker and get the whistle before midnight.
NO LONGER: Mister Tibbersnatch, the peddler, holds Tod's shadow and seven other children's in a jar.
NO LONGER: Tibbersnatch carries the jar with him and leaves at midnight.
NO LONGER: He will hand over the jar for an old tin whistle, loved fifty years, its tune worn soft.

OPTIONS:
- Go back down to the square with the whistle to see whether the peddler still wants it (for: finishing the trade for the shadows)
- Fetch a poker and climb to the gearloft anyway (for: making sure the clock can't strike thirteen)
* Put the whistle back in Ambrose's hand and tell him the shadows are free without it (for: settling what I owe him and keeping Maudie's whistle where it belongs)
DO: I hold the whistle out to Ambrose, slow. "Ambrose. The shadows are loose, and the children are waking, yawning and grumpy, each with a shadow behind them. Hester pulled the cork, so the peddler never needed this. Fair's fair, it's yours. Take it back." I wait with my hand open until he closes his fingers on it.
JOURNAL: He gave me a gift that cost him, and I'd have owed him for it. Handing it back square leaves nothing hanging between us, and it's Maudie's anyway. After this I'll still fetch a poker and watch the clock until midnight, and then see about four walls of my own.

OPTIONS:
- Head south to the Lopsided Square with the whistle and find the peddler, to trade it for the jar of shadows (for: getting the children's shadows back)
- Go round the hearths for a poker and climb to the gearloft to jam the Great Gear (for: making sure the clock can't strike thirteen)
* Tell Ambrose I'll pay him back in coal for the whistle, and ask whether the clock is still running fast (for: settling what I owe him and learning if the danger is truly past)
DO: I close my hand slow round the whistle and say, "Ambrose. You said keep the buttons, and I'll not argue. But fair's fair, I owe you, and I'll bring coal for that cold hearth of yours, no charge. Is she still running fast? If she is, I'll go up the ladder with a poker before midnight."
JOURNAL: Ambrose gave me his Maudie's whistle for nothing, and that sits heavy on me, so I'll square it with coal, the one thing I carry well. I'll still keep the poker and the gearloft in mind till I know the clock's safe, and I'm working toward the shadows home, the thirteenth stroke stopped, and no debts left on my tally.
